observations: Photo 0 shows a black PlayStation 4 console on a white surface, with a monitor displaying the PS4 home screen. The console has 'PS4' embossed on the front right side.
The monitor screen shows game icons including 'My Friend Pedro - Blood Bullets Bananas', 'AOTENNS 2', 'Trials Fusion', and others. The user is 'User1'.
Photo 1 shows the same setup, with game icons including 'FIFA 23', 'Werewolf: The Apocalypse', 'Mortal Kombat Ultimate', and a Spider-Man icon. The monitor brand is Lenovo.

Photo 2 shows the same setup, with game icons including 'Warhammer Chaosbane', 'AOTENNS 2', 'Trials Fusion', and 'Tennis Effect'. The screen also shows 'Enter', 'To the Left End', 'To the Right End', 'Options Menu' at the bottom.
All photos show the same console and monitor setup. The console appears to be a standard PS4 model, not a slim or Pro variant.
The seller claims the console is 'hacked with raspberry/ or pico' and has 'two controllers' and 'games fully installed'.
No controllers are visible in any photo.
The games shown on screen are a mix of legitimate titles and some that appear to be pirated or modified (e.g., 'AOTENNS 2' instead of 'AO Tennis 2', 'Tennis Effect' instead of 'Tennis World Tour').

claims.evidence: The screen shows games that appear to be pirated or modified, which suggests hacking, but there is no direct visual proof of a Raspberry Pi or Pico device. The console itself looks standard.
No controllers are visible in any of the photos. The claim cannot be verified from the images.
The screen shows multiple game icons, including 'FIFA 23', 'Werewolf: The Apocalypse', 'Warhammer Chaosbane', etc., indicating games are installed and accessible.

Hidden risks related to piracy, functionality, and accessories require additional proof before pricing can be determined.
